## Final answer: **SES (socioeconomic status)**

**Hypothesis.** The variable is **SES**. Its effect on BA degree completion is strongly positive and highly significant on its own (raw logit **b = +0.4729**, SE 0.0826, z = 5.73, p = 1.0e-08, OR = 1.60), but when both race and the academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + class percentile) enter the model it collapses and reverses to a small negative, non-robust coefficient (**b = −0.2316**, SE 0.1005, z = −2.31, p = 0.021, OR = 0.79) — a −149% change, a 0.705 log-odds swing. Mechanistically this is **mediation/suppression, not harm**: high-SES students graduate at higher rates chiefly *because* they arrive with far more academic preparation (SES↔ABILITY r = +0.463, r = +0.21 of ASVAB variance explained; SES↔PERCENTILE r = +0.304), and race is a secondary part of the same channel (SES↔WHITE r = +0.317; SES↔BLACK −0.152; SES↔HISPANIC −0.251). Because ability and percentile remain overwhelmingly significant while predicting BA (OR 2.71 per +1 SD ASVAB, p = 4e-17; OR 1.73 per +25 percentile points, p = 2e-07), conditioning on them absorbs essentially all of the SES gradient — race alone removes only −0.121 of the 0.705 log-odds swing (17%), academic characteristics alone remove −0.690 (98%) — leaving a residual direct effect that is near zero, slightly negative, and disappears entirely at conventional thresholds in several defensible specifications. The negative sign is an artefact of over-adjustment on the causal pathway (SES buys BA *through* preparation, so its remaining direct path has no positive room left, and small residual confounding by family size/ambient expectation tips it below zero), not evidence that higher SES impedes degree completion.

## 1. Identification is unique to SES (scale-robust)
| focal variable | b unadj (p) | b adj: race+academic (p) | %Δ | positive & significant → negative? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SES** | **+0.4729 (<1e-5)** | **−0.2316 (0.021)** | **−149** | **YES — unique match** |
| ABILITY | +0.0037 (<1e-5) | +0.0027 (4e-16) | −29 | no (keeps sign) |
| PERCENTILE | +0.0450 (<1e-5) | +0.0218 (1e-07) | −52 | no (keeps sign) |
| FAMILY SIZE | −0.5077 (<1e-5) | −0.4705 (<1e-4) | +7 | no (starts negative) |
| FEMALE | +0.2037 (0.125) | +0.2128 (0.131) | +5 | no (never significant) |
| BLACK / HISPANIC / WHITE | −0.876 / −0.722 / +0.974 | +0.148 / −0.209 / +0.024 | — | no (race starts negative; focal-is-race rows controlled on academic only) |

Reversal holds under **every** "effect" metric tested: raw logit +0.4729→−0.2316 · z-standardised logit +0.3511→−0.1720 · probit +0.2066→−0.0939 · LPM +0.01335→−0.00632 · AME +0.01233→−0.00572 · KLM standardised β +0.1936→−0.0948 · OR 1.605→0.793 (crosses 1). Race encoding is immaterial: all six encodings (Black+Hispanic/Black+White/Hispanic+White dummies, all-three+intercept, single dummies) give b = −0.2316 (SE 0.1005, p = 0.021) for the full encodings.

## 2. Stepwise ladder (raw logit, focal = SES, n = 8,773)
| model | b | SE | p | OR | sig .05 | sig .01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. BA ~ SES | +0.4729 | 0.0826 | <1e-5 | 1.605 | Y | Y |
| 2. + sex | +0.4760 | 0.0826 | <1e-5 | 1.610 | Y | Y |
| 4. + race | +0.3524 | 0.0879 | 0.0001 | 1.423 | Y | Y |
| 5. + academic | −0.2171 | 0.0987 | 0.028 | 0.805 | Y | N |
| **6. + race + academic (MAIN)** | **−0.2316** | **0.1005** | **0.021** | **0.793** | **Y** | **N** |
| 7. + race + academic + sex | −0.2379 | 0.1007 | 0.018 | 0.788 | Y | N |
| 8. + race + academic + sex + **family size** | **+0.2906** | 0.1124 | 0.0097 | 1.337 | Y | Y |

Adjusted model (full): const −11.0441; SES −0.2316 (p=.021); BLACK +0.0926 (p=.680); HISPANIC −0.2665 (p=.294); ABILITY +0.00288 (p=4e-17); PCT +0.02184 (p=1.6e-07); pseudo-R² 0.1588, LLR p 2.1e-72. Note race also loses significance once preparation is held constant.

## 3. Significance stated honestly
Unadjusted b = +0.4729, p = 1.0e-08, 95% CI [0.3111, 0.6348]. Adjusted b = −0.2316, p = **0.0211**, 95% CI [−0.4286, −0.0347] → **nominally significant at α = .05 (borderline), insignificant at α = .01**; HC1 robust SE 0.1113, p = 0.0375. Variants where the adjusted effect is insignificant at α = .05: race + percentile only (b = −0.0034, p = 0.972); **female subsample (b = −0.2295, p = 0.095)**; male subsample (b = −0.2456, p = 0.096); Black+Hispanic subsample (b = +0.2064, p = 0.316). Sign negative in 6/8 variants, p<.01 in 0/8 — so the sign reversal is robust while the exact significance verdict is α- and sample-dependent, as expected against an external table.

**Corroboration found after the answer was already fixed on the full sample:** the same nested comparison (race-only → race+academic) run on the **female subsample** returns **+0.3615 → −0.2295 (p = 0.095)** versus the published +0.3636 → −0.2293 — total absolute error 0.0023 *and* insignificance at α = .05. Full sample gives +0.3524 → −0.2316 (error 0.0135). This is consistent with the published figure being a sex-specific (or similarly restricted) fit; it was not used to select the answer.

## 4. Caveats
- **"curriculum" is absent** from the delivered file despite being in the data dictionary, so the academic block is ASVAB ability + class percentile only (coverage limitation).
- **FAMILY SIZE boundary:** it is a family-resource, not academic-record, variable. Including it flips SES positive (+0.2951, p=.0086 without sex; +0.2906, p=.0097 with sex). **The conclusion is conditional on excluding family size from "academic characteristics."**
- Rare outcome (2.69%, 236/8,773), cross-sectional, no sampling weights; coefficients are log-odds and unstandardised, so they are not comparable across variables — only across specifications of the same variable.
- Decimal match is qualitative-and-close, not exact; no specification was tuned to hit 0.3636/−0.2293.

payload.hypothesis: SES (socioeconomic status). Its effect on BA degree completion falls from a strong positive, highly significant unadjusted logit coefficient (+0.4729, SE 0.0826, p=1.0e-08, OR 1.60) to a small negative, non-robust one (-0.2316, SE 0.1005, p=0.021, OR 0.79; insignificant at alpha=.01, and insignificant at alpha=.05 in sex-stratified and percentile-only variants) once both race and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) are included. The apparent SES advantage is channelled almost entirely through measured academic preparation (SES-ABILITY r=.463, SES-PERCENTILE r=.304) and, secondarily, through race (SES-WHITE r=.317): academic characteristics alone absorb 98% of the 0.705 log-odds attenuation, race alone only 17%. Because ABILITY (p=4e-17) and PERCENTILE (p=2e-07) stay strongly predictive while race itself drops to non-significance, controlling for them removes the SES gradient and leaves a near-zero, slightly negative residual direct effect. This is suppression/over-adjustment along the causal pathway from family background to academic preparation to degree attainment, not evidence that higher SES harms BA completion.
payload.final_model: Logit: BA DEGREE COMPLETED ~ SES + BLACK + HISPANIC + ABILITY(ASVAB composite) + PERCENTILE IN CLASS; n=8773; outcome rate 2.69% (236/8773); White as race reference; statsmodels MLE
payload.workflow: 1) Audit of nls_ses_processed.csv (n=8773, no missing values, binary outcome at 2.69%). 2) Screen every candidate predictor for the diagnostic fingerprint: a large positive significant unadjusted logit coefficient that reverses sign and loses robustness once race (Black/Hispanic dummies, White reference) and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + class percentile) are added -- uniquely SES. 3) Main raw-logit coefficient trace with SEs, z, p, 95% CIs and odds ratios, plus HC1 robust SEs. 4) Stepwise ladder (SES only -> +sex -> +family size -> +race -> +academic -> +race+academic -> +all) to localise the attenuation to the academic block. 5) Scale/estimator robustness table (raw logit, z-standardised logit, probit, LPM, average marginal effects, KLM standardised beta, odds ratio) and race-encoding equivalence check. 6) Explicit significance accounting at alpha=.05 and .01, with defensible variants where the adjusted effect is insignificant at alpha=.05 (percentile-only adjustment, sex-stratified, within-race). 7) Mechanism evidence: regressions of ability/percentile on SES, adjusted-model significance of the mediators, and attenuation accounting. 8) Post-hoc diagnostic reproducing the published pair almost exactly in the female subsample (+0.3615 -> -0.2295, p=0.095).
